segment:
Mara took two steps toward them, trying to look relaxed, wondering whether she should put her phone down before anyone else arrived and expecting that Jonah would introduce her any moment. Instead the brown-haired fellow turned toward her with the same unsmiling expression and held out a hand.
She was about to reach for it when Jonah stepped in between them—literally, stepping to the left in front of her.
“You already know Mara,” he said.
There was no reason for him to say that: neither of the two men had met Mara before today. They hadn’t even been there when she and Jonah had arrived. She wasn’t sure if Jonah was joking, and neither did the brown-haired man. Mara noticed his eyes flit from her to Jonah’s face and back again, trying to work out why Jonah said such a thing, until Mara simply offered her own hand instead.

“Mara,” she said with a small smile. “Hello.”
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

And that was when a door opened down the hallway behind her, releasing two voices into the room. One female, one male; one asking a question, the other replying; neither loud nor excited, just casual conversation. Jonah released her hand and turned away to look down the hall at them.
When Mara heard the voices and followed his gaze, she saw one young man who wasn’t Jonah, but close in size and shape; he had brown hair and a beard and was carrying a glass.

The brown-haired man glanced once over his shoulder, saw them standing there, nodded hello, and stepped right into the gathering, holding up his glass of wine—a half-full plastic cup with the Fulcrum logo on it. “Cheers.” He set it on the table against the wall to the left of the door, and stepped forward to shake Jonah’s hand as they exchanged names.

Mara noticed his eyes flit from her to Jonah’s face and back again, trying to work out why Jonah said such a thing, until Mara simply offered her own hand instead.

“Mara,” she said with a small smile. “Hello.”

segment:
The brown-haired man was a visiting fellow who was staying at the retreat center while writing a book on psychology, Jonah told her—which was how she learned Jonah’s last name too; the brown-haired man was doing a project on Reed’s theories about the language of gesture. He said something else that made Jonah laugh and lean forward.
They fell back into easy conversation right in the doorway. They all seemed to be in their late twenties or early thirties, although she might have guessed Jonah was closer to twenty when she walked in—and now, talking to this other man, his posture held its weight easily on his feet, his chin up and shoulders down. They chatted in small groups about books and philosophy, without seeming to notice the glass sitting there, forgotten, on the table by the door.

segment:
Jonah greeted him warmly and waved Mara over to introduce them. His visitor shook her hand and asked her where she was from, and then asked about Jonah—apparently they had known each other since college, which Mara found interesting and a little disquieting. It was a surprise that Jonah had already been in this place for that long and she had never heard of him before, or of any of his research.
The visitor started to pour himself more wine from the bottle that stood by his plastic cup, when a hand rose beside him on the wall—an elderly woman’s hand, strong but lined. She put a finger around the lip of the cup, lifted it, and slid it off the table onto the tray she was holding out with her other hand. The man didn’t seem to notice at first, or maybe didn’t acknowledge noticing, just kept talking and reaching for his refill. The woman waited with the tray until the conversation had paused and then quietly passed by to clear it away.
Mara watched her go.

segment:
Jonah kept an eye on Mara as the man introduced himself as Daniel. They spoke for a moment about nothing in particular. The brown-haired man turned to Mara and took her hand between both his, and then turned back to Jonah with some comment about the wine; Jonah smiled politely, but then Mara felt him moving toward her. As he approached, Jonah offered up another greeting. “You are the first, or are more arriving?”
“I’m first.” Mara’s eyes rose from Jonah’s hands to his face, to find herself under his gaze. He had a very open expression as he looked directly at her and continued, “This is Daniel, our visiting fellow this month.” The words were addressed to her, and yet the gaze remained locked on hers.
“Hello,” she replied again.

Mara found that she still couldn’t take her eyes off of Jonah, despite being close enough to him that if she turned her head at all, he would be outside her field of vision.
“I’ll show you your room,” he said suddenly. “I’m assuming you’re here to stay.”

segment:
The brown-haired man had raised his own glass now. “Mara, nice to meet you.”
She smiled and accepted his handshake. “I’ve never been here before.”
“It’s beautiful, isn’t it?” said the brown-haired man. “And comfortable. The couches are great to lie down on—like a hammock.”

The conversation drifted on to the visiting scholar’s subject area as Mara stood at the back of the room near the doorway and listened; she’d always found it hard to listen when people had already been talking. But she had just found out that the younger man’s name was Jonah Reed, which made him another piece of Fulcrum’s public face that she was beginning to see in person for the first time.
She took a step back so she could watch his face.

segment:
“It was good to meet you in person,” said Mara when it was her turn to introduce herself, “and to have confirmation that Fulcrum hasn’t turned entirely into a fraternity.” She didn’t know him at all and could not have guessed how his sense of humor worked, but she took a chance, hoping that he’d be amused. He was; his eyebrows raised a fraction.
She watched Jonah’s face in turn, studying his expression for reaction while the new arrival spoke.
The visiting fellow had a smooth, slightly high-pitched voice that sounded almost too educated in the first few syllables—the sort of voice she associated with NPR fundraisers.
“How long have you been here?” he asked Jonah as they both moved forward to join her.
